meta.title: GMCP to Web Client
meta.subtitle: One step in the world rebuilds a map snapshot, filters it against the rooms this character has actually walked, and pushes it to the browser as a single GMCP payload

views.label: Every move sends a map
views.note: A move queues a RoomChange event. The Zone module answers it for that one user, and drops the event when a mob moved and no user id is set.

views.label: Fog is enforced on the server
views.note: Snapshot walks the crawled graph and skips every room that is not in the visited set, so an unwalked room never reaches the payload.

views.label: The GMCP payload
views.note: One JSON push per move: zone name, current floor, party room ids, and the surviving rooms with their classified exits.

views.label: Drawing the map
views.note: The browser handler calls setZoneSnapshot, which keeps only the current floor, places rooms by x and y, then draws the edges.

views.label: Party markers and exit types
views.note: Exit flags choose the stroke: locked doors, secret dashes, one way arrows, arch gates, biome roads. A party room gets a small figure.

cards.title: One step, one snapshot
items: A successful move records the room on the character and queues a RoomChange event
The Zone module answers that event, so the map is rebuilt from scratch on every step
A mob move raises the same event with no user id and is dropped before any work
The current room is force added to the visited set, because the mark and the event race

cards.title: What the fog filter actually does
items: Snapshot iterates the crawled graph and skips any room id absent from the visited set
Nothing about an unwalked room is built: no coordinates, no title, no biome, no tags
Ephemeral instance rooms are skipped as well, so a dungeon copy id cannot leak out
The filter runs before the payload exists, so the browser has nothing to filter
The dimming you see in the client is distance shading only, not a second fog check

cards.title: The honest edge of the fog
items: An exit from a room you HAVE walked is still sent when its far side is unwalked
That stub carries a direction, the destination room id, and the door flags on it
It also carries the destination zone name when the exit crosses a zone boundary
A secret exit out of a visited room is flagged secret whether or not you found it
This matches the ASCII map, which has always drawn the same question mark stub

cards.title: What the browser is given
items: Zone name, the current floor, party room ids, and the surviving rooms with exits
Party data is room ids only, self excluded, de duplicated, instance ids translated
Rooms on other floors you have walked are sent, and the client draws one floor at a time
Exit flags drive the stroke: locked, secret, one way, gate, vertical tick, biome road
